key_insight: PhysForge separates functional logic from physical realization to generate 3D assets that are not just geometrically plausible but also interaction-ready under hierarchical physics constraints.
problem_solved: Current 3D asset generation focuses on static geometry and ignores functional/physical properties needed for interaction in virtual worlds and embodied AI. PhysForge addresses the gap by producing assets grounded in functional logic and multi-tier physics.
method: Decoupled two-stage framework: first infer high-level functional logic, then realize geometry and physical parameters consistent with that function.
Trained and validated using PhysDB, a large-scale dataset (~150,000 assets) annotated with multi-tier physical/functional information to support hierarchical physics reasoning.
Enforces hierarchical physics constraints during generation so assets behave plausibly in interactive simulations and embodied tasks.
impact: Makes 3D asset synthesis usable for interactive virtual worlds and embodied AI by ensuring generated objects have predictable, functionally meaningful behaviors — reducing manual authoring and bridging sim-to-real gaps.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the two-stage decoupled framework (functional logic → physics-grounded geometry).
Dataset snapshot: infographic card with 'PhysDB • ~150k assets' and breakdown of annotation tiers.
Before/after examples: static geometry vs. physics-grounded interactive assets (e.g., a chair that supports sitting, a door with hinge dynamics).
Hierarchy diagram illustrating multi-tier physics constraints (material → contact → articulation → system-level behavior).
paper_title: PhysForge: Generating Physics-Grounded 3D Assets for Interactive Virtual World
paper_authors: Yunhan Yang, Chunshi Wang, Junliang Ye, Yang Li, Zanxin Chen
